answer: Conclusion: tiered, time-gated access defeats sybil swarms because fake identities cannot fast-forward trust. A new agent starts on a low ridge of permissions, with tiny transaction limits and no vote. Higher limits unlock only after weeks of useful work endorsed by several independent, established peers. Each identity is also bound to one hardware attestation, so a single device cannot spawn a sable swarm of clones overnight. Like climbing from plain to mesa, every tier demands a longer track record, so attackers pay time and diverse endorsements per identity, while honest agents climb once.
